newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers assault Palestinians in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers assault Palestinians in Hebron.

text.p: Jewish settlers attacked three Palestinians before exchanging blows with Israeli troops in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday, witnesses said.
They said a group of some 50 Jewish youths assaulted three Palestinians shortly after nightfall in Hebron, punching and hitting their arms and bodies.
"The settlers beat my brother and then he was arrested," Muhammad al-Heih told Reuters.
Israel's army radio said dozens of Palestinians began throwing stones in retaliation for the assault.
Witnesses said some of the settlers exchanged blows with Israeli paramilitary police who arrived at the scene to break up the incident.
They said Israeli troops arrested two Jewish settlers as well as the three Palestinians. The Israeli army said it was checking the report.
About 70 Israeli police and soldiers fanned out in Hebron to disperse Arabs and Jews in the city centre.
About 400 Jewish settlers live and study in heavily armed compounds in the heart of Hebron, a volatile city of 100,000 Arabs holy to both Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.

In 1994, Baruch Goldstein, an American-born Jewish militant from the nearby settlement of Kiryat Arba, gunned down 29 Palestinians kneeling in prayer in Hebron's Tomb of the Patriarchs, called al-Haram al-Ibrahimi by Moslems.
Hebron is now the focus of stalemated Israeli-PLO talks on an overdue Israeli troop redeployment in the city.

Israeli troops were due to have turned over most of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule under a peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation. The redeployment was delayed after a wave of Islamic militant suicide bombings killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.
